title: Ability Scores
markdown:
# Ability Scores

Six abilities provide a quick description of every creature's physical and mental characteristics:

- **Strength** — physical power, athletic training, and raw force.
- **Dexterity** — agility, reflexes, and balance.
- **Constitution** — health, stamina, and vital force.
- **Intelligence** — memory, reasoning, and analytical thinking.
- **Wisdom** — awareness, intuition, and willpower.
- **Charisma** — confidence, eloquence, and leadership.

## Ability Modifiers

Each ability score generates a **modifier** ranging from −5 (for a score of 1) to +10 (for a score of 30). The average humanoid has a score of 10 in every ability (+0 modifier). The modifier is applied to most d20 rolls involving that ability.

| Score | Modifier |
|---|---|
| 1 | −5 |
| 8–9 | −1 |
| 10–11 | +0 |
| 12–13 | +1 |
| 14–15 | +2 |
| 16–17 | +3 |
| 18–19 | +4 |
| 20 | +5 |

## Advantage and Disadvantage

The 5e engine resolves contested or chance-based tasks by rolling **2d20** and using the higher (advantage) or the lower (disadvantage) result. Sources of advantage and disadvantage cancel each other out — if you have both from any cause, you roll a single d20 normally.

## Saving Throws

A **saving throw** represents an attempt to resist a spell, trap, poison, disease, or similar threat. You roll 1d20, add the relevant ability modifier, and add your **proficiency bonus** if you are proficient in that save.

## Proficiency Bonus

Your **proficiency bonus** scales with character level: +2 at level 1, +3 at level 5, +4 at level 9, +5 at level 13, and +6 at level 17. It applies to things you have trained in: attacks with weapons you know, skills you have chosen, saves you are proficient in, and the DC of spells you cast.

## Skills

Skills are specialized applications of your abilities. See the **Skills** section in the sidebar for the complete list and which ability each one uses.
